meta.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch decision, packaging and price
meta.subtitle: Discussion document for the CEO and executive team, January 2027 planning
meta.purpose: Decide whether to launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 and how to package and price it
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data; all figures from the briefing pack

inputs.label: Design choice made on the user's behalf (user unavailable)
inputs.content: Pro includes 600 AI requests per seat per month; overage priced so an account at 6,800 requests pays $149 a month

storyline.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, and in Q2 if Q4 win rates confirm the Routewise threat

exec_summary.text: Copilot helps dispatchers, but paid demand is far below the survey: a $149 add-on would add about $2.5M of ARR, not $8M

sub_points.text: Beta accounts scheduled 11% more jobs per dispatcher-hour, but they were volunteers
14% of beta accounts bought at $149, compared with 46% of survey respondents who said they would
At the paywall rate, the add-on brings under a third of the $8M forecast

exec_summary.text: A Pro plan at $12 more per seat, with 600 requests per seat included, reaches more accounts and keeps margin above 75%

sub_points.text: A flat $149 fee draws heavy users: the top tenth would cost $131 a month to serve
At the 2023 tier's 33% take-up, Pro adds about $2.9M of ARR, against $2.5M for the add-on
The NRR target needs 26% take-up; uncapped, margin breaks at 5,300 requests per account

exec_summary.text: Timing turns on Routewise: launch in Q2 if Q4 win rates stay near 37%, and rewrite mobile first if they recover

sub_points.text: Routewise's AI puts at most about $0.6M of new ARR a year at risk
Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, 4.5 times as much as AI
Delaying Copilot costs more only if Routewise's AI, not its discount, is taking deals

next_steps.action: Read Q4 2026 win rates in Routewise deals and pick Plan A (launch first) or Plan B (mobile first)
Approve Pro at $12 more per seat with 600 requests per seat and overage at $0.024
Offer Pro to a random sample of non-beta accounts to test take-up against the 26% threshold
Build allowance metering, overage billing and a monthly margin and take-up dashboard
Renegotiate the inference contract before it expires

constraints.item: Company gross margin at or above 75%
constraints.effect: Pro holds at 76.0% at beta mean usage but breaks above about 5,300 requests per account uncapped; the 600-per-seat allowance with overage keeps 75.3% even at 6,800 for every account. Free in Core breaks it (73.5% at median usage)

constraints.item: Inference cost of $0.009 per request (fixed through December 2027) and $0.6M a year of platform cost
constraints.effect: Netted out in every contribution and margin figure; the add-on's headline ARR is gross, which slide 1.3 states

constraints.item: 14 engineers for two quarters ($1.47M) and a two-quarter delay to the mobile rewrite
constraints.effect: Weighed as lifetime gross profit with churned accounts lost for good; the governing thought makes the Q2 date conditional
Pro reaches it alone only at 26% take-up or more; the low case does not. Competitive new-logo ARR does not count towards NRR

alternatives.option: Mobile rewrite first, Copilot launched in Q4 2027
alternatives.why: Cheaper if Routewise's discount, not its AI, explains the win-rate fall (then mobile first wins once the rewrite fixes over 8% of mobile churn); it becomes Plan B, chosen on the Q4 win-rate read-out
Survey intent is 3.3 times actual purchase; $2.5M ARR at best, and heavy users self-select

alternatives.option: Include Copilot free in Core to match Routewise
alternatives.why: Gross margin falls to 73.5%, below the 75% floor, with no new ARR

alternatives.option: Overage at a full 75% margin ($0.036 per request)
alternatives.why: Would charge the proven paywall buyers about $185 a month against $149 today; $0.024 keeps them at about $149 and the company above 75%

failure_threshold.driver: share of accounts that move to Pro
failure_threshold.threshold: below about 26% Pro alone misses the NRR target; timing separately flips at 60% (AI is the cause) or 8% (discount is the cause) of mobile churn fixed
failure_threshold.range: NRR uplift low / base / high: 2.1 / 5.0 / 7.0 percentage points at 14% / 33% / 46% take-up

consistency.headline: Launch Copilot in 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, and in Q2 if Q4 win rates confirm the Routewise threat
consistency.fix: Changed from an unconditional Q2 launch: the earlier draft compared churn lost for good with revenue that is only delayed; on a like-for-like basis the Q2 date depends on the Q4 win-rate read-out

Timing: let Q4 win rates set the order

slides.rationale: Three beta outcomes, each against its matched benchmark -> kpi-big-numbers

lead_message.text: Copilot does make dispatchers more productive, but a volunteer beta overstates how much the whole base will gain

slides.unit_line: **Dispatch Copilot beta outcomes**, 240 volunteer accounts, 12 weeks, 2026

items.caption: dispatcher hours saved per week, self-reported
drivers: Schedule proposals and quote drafts take over routine office work
Self-reported figures tend to run high; no time study backs them
Beta accounts have 8.1 seats on average, so more hours to save than a typical account

items.caption: jobs scheduled per dispatcher-hour
drivers: The one measured gain: 5.5 times the change in matched accounts
Compared with the prior 12 weeks, so seasonality is partly netted out
Measured on volunteers, which the pack lists as an open uncertainty

items.caption: 90-day renewal rate, beta accounts
drivers: Points to a retention benefit, the lever NRR needs
Volunteers are more active and would likely renew more anyway
Too short a window to size a churn effect, so the case below leaves it out

footnotes: Matched non-beta accounts are the comparison set in the briefing pack; beta accounts volunteered and are larger and more active than the base

body.assumptions_header: Even $2.5M is an upper estimate, for three reasons
assumptions: The 14% comes from volunteers that are larger and more active than the base; take-up across all accounts is likely lower
The forecast's 46% is stated intent from a 6% response rate, skewed to larger accounts
No discounts, and buyers stay for the full year
Gross revenue before inference cost; buyers are heavy users (next section)

footnotes: The CPO forecast recomputed: 9,800 accounts × 46% × $149 × 12 = $8.06M, the 'about $8M' in the proposal

body.assumptions_header: The estimate rests on three assumptions
assumptions: A third of accounts move to Pro within a year, as 33% did after the 2023 higher-tier launch; Pro includes Copilot, the earlier tier did not
Accounts that move have the base average of 6.2 seats and pay $12 more per seat per month
No change in Core churn or seat counts from the launch; all new ARR comes from existing accounts, so it counts towards NRR

slides.so_what: An average account pays $74.4 a month for Pro, half the $149 add-on, and Pro costs less for any account under 12.4 seats
footnotes: The 2023 tier did not include AI; whether Copilot pulls more or fewer accounts up is the main uncertainty (next page)

lead_message.text: Pro meets the NRR target on its own as long as at least about 26% of accounts move up

sidebar.header: The case turns on one number: Pro take-up
sidebar.caption: of accounts must move to Pro for it to close the NRR gap alone
bullets: **Low, at the paywall's 14%:** Pro falls short, and NRR needs other levers such as lower mobile churn
**Base, at the 2023 tier's 33%:** clears the target with room to spare
**High, at the survey's 46%:** an upper bound, since the survey overstated intent

slides.rationale: Win rate before and after Routewise's launch -> column, with the ARR at stake in the sidebar

lead_message.text: At most about $0.6M of new ARR a year rides on Routewise's AI, a third of the sales memo's claim

slides.unit_line: **Brightwork win rate in deals where Routewise competed**, %, 2026

sidebar.header: Whether AI caused the fall is still open
sidebar.caption: new ARR a year if Copilot won back the whole fall
bullets: **Q3 2026:** Routewise launched AI and offered 20% off the first year at once, so the fall has two possible causes
**The memo:** counts every loss note that mentions AI as a deal Copilot would win, about $1.8M a year
**New logos only:** this ARR does not count towards NRR; Q4 2026 win rates will show which cause holds

basis.header: How we sized the ARR at stake

terms.caption: new ARR a year at most

footnotes: Memo-implied ARR: 1,560 opportunities × 63% lost × 31% of loss notes mentioning AI × $5,878 = $1.79M a year

slides.rationale: Ranking of churn reasons -> bar-ranking, mobile highlighted

lead_message.text: The real cost of launching is the mobile delay: app reliability drives 27% of churn, 4.5 times as much as AI

slides.unit_line: **Main reason given by accounts that churned**, % of churned accounts, n = 1,190, 2026

sidebar.header: Mobile, not AI, is what customers leave over
sidebar.caption: as many churned accounts cite mobile as cite AI
bullets: **Mobile reliability:** about $2.18M of ARR lost a year (14% churn × 27% × $57.6M), against $0.48M for AI
**Feature requests:** a reliable mobile app ranks first for twice as many customers as AI scheduling
**The trade-off:** Copilot's 14 engineers push the rewrite back two quarters

footnotes: ARR figures assume churned accounts are of average size; 2026 customer survey: 38% rank a reliable mobile app first, 19% AI scheduling

slides.rationale: Cost of each delay under each condition, one measure -> bar chart, Copilot cases highlighted

lead_message.text: Delaying Copilot is the costlier choice only if Routewise's AI, rather than its discount, is taking our deals
highlights: Copilot waits: AI is taking deals
Copilot waits: discount explains the fall

slides.unit_line: **Lifetime gross profit lost by a two-quarter delay**, $ millions

sidebar.header: The cause of the win-rate fall decides the order
bullets: **AI taking deals:** a Copilot delay loses deals and accounts for good, so launch first
**Discount the cause:** a Copilot delay only defers Pro revenue, so mobile first wins once the rewrite fixes 8% of mobile churn

basis.header: How the Copilot bars are built

footnotes: Mobile bars: churn ARR × share fixed × $5.57; the pack does not say how much churn the rewrite fixes
ARR lost for good = half a year of lost deals and AI-reason churn; $5.57 = 78% margin ÷ 14% churn (7.1-year life); AI effects are upper bounds

slides.rationale: Two dated plans and the decision that picks between them -> timeline-roadmap

lead_message.text: A January read of fourth-quarter win rates picks the order of work; either way Pro launches in 2027

bars.label: 14 engineers build Pro; launch in Q2
Rewrite restarts with the launch team
Pro price test on non-beta accounts

slides.so_what: Our default is Plan A: the win-rate fall and AI loss notes point to Routewise's AI, but the Q4 data should confirm it
footnotes: Either plan costs 14 engineers × $210K × half a year = $1.47M (23% of the 60 engineers); provider list prices fell 35% in the past 12 months

Plan A if the Q4 2026 win rate in Routewise deals stays near 37%; Plan B if it recovers toward 44%. Plan B timing assumes the rewrite takes the same two quarters the delay would have cost; the pack does not give its full length
